claims.text: Current guideline: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI guideline for acute coronary syndromes.
claims.quote: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes

claims.text: It brings together the 2013 STEMI guideline and the 2014 NSTE-ACS guideline.
claims.quote: incorporates new evidence since the "2013 ACCF/AHA Guideline for the Management of ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction" and the corresponding "2014 AHA/ACC Guideline for the Management of Patients With Non-ST-Elevation Acute Coronary Syndromes"
ECG is the most important test and should be performed as soon as possible (within 10 minutes of presentation to medical care, whether in or out of the hospital)

claims.text: STEMI: ST elevation ≥ 1 mm in 2 or more contiguous leads.
claims.quote: For STEMI, initial ECG is usually diagnostic, showing ST-segment elevation ≥ 1 mm in 2 or more contiguous leads subtending the damaged area

claims.text: Leads V2–V3: elevation must be 1.5 to 2.5 mm, depending on age and gender.
claims.quote: In leads V2-V3 the elevation must be 1.5 to 2.5 mm depending on age and gender.

claims.text: NSTEMI ECG: horizontal or downsloping ST depression, T-wave inversion, transient ST elevation.
claims.quote: Typical ECG findings in NSTEMI include: Horizontal or downsloping ST depression T wave inversion Transient ST elevation

claims.text: Troponin timing: hs-cTn at presentation and 1 to 2 hours later; standard cTn at 0 and 3 to 6 hours.
claims.quote: Patients suspected of having an acute coronary syndrome should have an hs-cTn assay performed on presentation and again 1 to 2 hours later. Troponin should be measured at 0 and 3 to 6 hours if a standard cTn assay is used.

claims.text: Don't wait for troponin in STEMI or an unstable NSTE-ACS.
claims.quote: Because troponin elevation lags behind the onset of myocardial injury, angiography and treatment in patients with STEMI, or unstable patients with a NSTE-ACS, should not be delayed because of an initially normal troponin level.
